decisions.location: Section 3 Data and Research Design, p. 7; Section 4.2, pp. 12-14; References, p. 20
decisions.quote:
Our pre-registered (see Appendix B.1 for blinded version) survey design builds
upon and replicates Magni (2021) and Alesina, Miano and Stantcheva (2023)
with a quota-representative (age, gender, education, region) sample of the sur-
vey company Kantar.
decisions.reason: Prior adjudication and state files are absent for this request. The paper conducts a pre-registered survey experiment in Germany (N = 1,587) that explicitly retests two distinct published priming studies: Magni (2021) (sibling target_index 0, which matches shipped row input_row_index 2261, DOI 10.1017/s0007123420000046, published online in 2020 and in print in 2021 in the British Journal of Political Science) and Alesina, Miano and Stantcheva (2023) (target_index 1, 'Immigration and redistribution.', The Review of Economic Studies 90(1):1-39; no DOI is printed in the source text). In Section 4.2 (Figure 4, Models 1-5), the authors empirically retest the immigration priming treatment and causal chain of Alesina, Miano and Stantcheva (2023), comparing their null effect of immigration priming on overall redistribution support and negative effect on welfare chauvinism against the original study's finding that immigration priming reduces support for redistribution. Shipped row 2261 represents only Magni (2020/2021), an independent study by a different author on inequality priming in Italy; report equivalence does not apply, so Alesina, Miano and Stantcheva (2023) is a genuinely missing original target.
